key_insight: A geometric invariant energy quadratization (IEQ) formulation enables curvature-driven surface evolution with unconditional discrete energy decay, independent of tangential motion.
engineering_relevance: The approach supports energy-stable finite element simulation of evolving interfaces governed by curvature-dependent energies.
method: Introduce a square-root auxiliary variable to express the geometric energy as a quadratic functional.
Use skew-symmetric surface transport so the energy law depends only on normal velocity.
Construct monolithic nonlinear parametric FEM schemes with BGN or minimal-deformation-rate tangential motion.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports unconditional discrete energy decay for both schemes and numerical experiments demonstrating robustness and accuracy, without quantitative results.
watch_item: Unconditional energy decay does not guarantee time-step-independent accuracy; the monolithic nonlinear schemes also require nonlinear solves.
paper_title: A geometric-IEQ approach for curvature-driven flows
